text:
eva: Heads up — kicking off a small program to retire a few of our fat RPC surfaces and replace them with narrow, well-tested facades. Goal: reduce coupling, lower hotpath tail latency, and make incremental paydown of tech debt possible. Quick sketch below.
meera: +1. Which surfaces are you targeting first?
jonathan: Curious about migration strategy — will we run dual-stack, or do consumers move lanes?
eva: Starting candidates: conductor-api (routing + orchestration), enricher-proxy (data enrichment pipeline), session-coordinator (session pinning + affinity). Proposal: phase 0 = interface audit + consumer mapping; phase 1 = extract read-only facades + contract tests; phase 2 = promote write paths + consumer cutovers; phase 3 = cut and remove old surface.
sam: How do we handle KV cache state and session affinity during cutover? Those are sticky.
meera: We should treat state as first-class: plan explicit ownership transfer, small sticky-shard experiments, and a shim that does read-through to old store during migration.
jonathan: Suggest cohortized migration by tenant: small internal tenants first, then mid, then top 10 production tenants. Canary signals: SLOs, error budget burn, and perf deltas.
riley: Timeline guess? This sounds multi-sprint. Need capacity planning.
eva: Rough estimate: 6–10 sprints across several teams if we do full safety nets. But we can deliver a useful read-only facade in 2–3 sprints for low-risk consumers.
meera: Tests we must gate on: contract tests (wire-level), perf benchmarks (p95/p99 token latency), synthetic load tests, and regression evals on critical prompt sets.
jonathan: Also: router fallback policy — if new facade fails, automatically route to old surface for N minutes while we fix. Need a circuit-breaker and observability hooks.
sam: Ops note: create dashboards for facade vs. old surface: request rate, p95/p99, error count, CPU/GPU utilization, and cache hit rate. Also add synthetic check that exercises session pinning.
eva: I'll spawn infra tickets. Dev-bot: please create the tracking epic and link infra/tasks.
dev-bot: Created epic INF-3142 and sub-tasks: INF-3142.1 interface-audit, INF-3142.2 read-facade-spike, INF-3142.3 router-fallback, INF-3142.4 canary-runbook — https://jira.internal/redwood/INF-3142
meera: We also need a migration checklist: consumer owners contacted, contract compliance signoff, perf baseline captured, canary rollback steps, and post-mortem template.
riley: Risk callouts: session-coordinator has heavy cross-service references; extraction may reveal hidden coupling. Plan for a 1-week safety freeze after each canary to monitor.
jonathan: One concrete snippet for the router fallback config (P.O.C):
```
routes:
  - match: /conductor.v1.Execute
    policy:
      primary: conductor-v2-facade
      fallback: conductor-v1
      failover_window: 120s
```
meera: Nice. Add a flag to enable wire-level logging during canary to help debug protocol drift.
eva: Action items: 1) interface audit (owners + callouts) 2) perf baseline + synthetic tests 3) router fallback implementation 4) canary runbook + tenant cohorts 5) schedule architecture deep-dive (1h). Who can join tomorrow 10am PT?
jonathan: I can.
meera: in
sam: me
riley: me
eva: Great — adding calendar invite. We'll put the audit doc in the architecture drive and tag owners in the JIRA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
meera: small follow-up — prefer to keep the initial facade read-only to reduce blast radius. We can iterate on writes after contract tests pass.
eva: Agreed. Read-only first, then write-phase with stricter gating.
jonathan: One more thing: notify Dedicated and Private infra teams early — there may be region-specific behavior.
eva: noted. I'll ping them in #eng-infra after the deep-dive.
sam: Also add a note to the release playbook about potential deployment order (control-plane before hotpath).
riley: Thanks — this feels actionable.
eva: Closing thread for now, will post notes after the meeting.
